original: Storage and movement occur over different timescales, so water does not follow one compulsory loop. A water budget compares inputs, outputs, and changes in storage within a defined area and time interval. Human activities can alter this balance. Paved surfaces often reduce infiltration and increase rapid runoff. Pumping removes groundwater, and sustained withdrawals greater than replenishment can reduce groundwater storage. Understanding these pathways helps explain how rainfall, underground reserves, and downstream water availability are connected.
